## Diagnosis Report

**Symptom entry (metric surface).** `GetAlerts()` returned 12 anomalies, all in the same window (2026‑01‑17 20:09:14–20:11:09): every boutique service shows a uniform traffic/throughput collapse (−65 % to −72 %), and three show latency explosions:

| Service | Latency | Node |
|---|---|---|
| frontend | p50 16.05 ms → **11 557.08 ms** (+71 921 %) | worker-01 |
| checkoutservice | p50 17.60 ms → **7 004.69 ms** (+39 696 %) | worker-01 |
| cartservice | p50 2.45 ms → **1 236.06 ms** (+50 450 %) | **worker-02** |

**Placement map (pods -o wide).** Six boutique pods sit on **worker-02** (cartservice, currencyservice, emailservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice, shippingservice); five on worker‑01 (frontend, adservice, checkoutservice, paymentservice, redis-cart).

**Localization.** The latency gradients follow *placement*, not traffic volume: `checkoutservice` (on w01) calls currencyservice + shippingservice + emailservice + cartservice — **all four on worker‑02** — which is why it is ~6× slower than cartservice alone; `frontend` (on w01) fans out to currencyservice, cartservice, productcatalogservice, recommendationservice — **also all on worker‑02** — hence its 11.5 s. Services that are *not* on worker‑02 and are not their callers (adservice, paymentservice, redis-cart) show only the secondary throughput drop. So worker‑02's network path is the single choke point.

**Node surface (close-out).** `DescribeResource(node/worker-02)`: `Ready=True` (KubeletReady), `NetworkUnavailable=False` (FlannelIsUp), no MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure, `Taints: <none>`, `Unschedulable: false`, allocatable 8 CPU / 15.6 GiB, allocated only 20 % CPU / 12 % memory. `GetClusterConfiguration()` shows worker‑02 identical to peer nodes — so this is **not** scheduling, capacity, cordon, taint, kubelet/containerd, or a missing service account.

**Mechanism.** The only node-scope anomaly in the whole snapshot is on worker‑02: `NETWORK_QUALITY_DEGRADED [TCP Retransmission] | Normal=0.00retrans -> Current=0.92retrans (New Spike)`. A sub‑1 retransmission/s spike is noise‑sized, not an order-of-magnitude loss regime — the classic delay signature (RTO breaches from high RTT, occurring where normal was 0.00). Corroboration: **no error logs** in frontend or cartservice, **all TCP connects succeed** (currencyservice:7000 and adservice:9555 both "Connection Succeeded"), and cartservice's own log stream is dense and steady (a request every ~50–100 ms, no stalls, no errors) while its *callers* measure 1.2 s — i.e. the application processes fine, and the time is spent on the wire out of worker‑02.

**Conclusion:** degraded network quality on **node/worker-02** — excessive network latency (with an incidental small TCP-retransmission spike) — explains the simultaneous latency inflation of services placed there and the cascade into checkoutservice/frontend, and the uniform throughput drop as the blocked frontend stops issuing requests.
